'''''Eierpunsch''''' (literally "egg punch") is the [[German language|German]] name given to a lukewarm, sweetened alcoholic egg-based drink.

==Ingredients==
*1 bottle (750 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:White Wine|white wine]]
*4 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]] (or 8 [[Cookbook:Egg Yolk|egg yolks]])
*5 tablespoons of [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*1 packet of [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla]] sugar (or 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] sugar plus 1 tsp vanilla extract)
*1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] of [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]]
*4 whole [[Cookbook:Clove|cloves]]
*250 ml strong brewed [[Cookbook:Tea|tea]], cooled
*[[Cookbook:Lemon|Lemon]] or lemon juice
*50 ml dark [[Cookbook:Rum|rum]] (optional)

==Procedure==

# [[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]] the 5 tablespoons of sugar into the eggs (or egg yolks), add a little cold white wine, and [[Cookbook:Beating|beat]] vigorously.
# Add the vanilla sugar to the mixture and pour in the remaining white wine, cinnamon, the cloves, lemon juice and the cooled tea. Add rum if using.
# Transfer the mixture to a pan and gently heat. Do not let the mixture heat too quickly or it will curdle. Before the mixture comes to the boil remove from the heat—the mixture should be foaming on top.
# Remove the cloves.
# Serve hot and foamy in a mug, optionally with [[Cookbook:Whipped Cream|whipped cream]] on top and a ginger biscuit.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* This recipe can also be made with red wine. If so, do not add 250 ml strong tea to the mixture. This will also affect the number of servings.
